chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Buraid al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

“For the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, and the private part and testicles of a free eunuch, one-third of the diyah is due. And for the private part of a young boy, the diyah is due in full.”

key_terms.ذَكَرِ ٱلْخَصِيِّ: the private part of a eunuch
key_terms.عَيْنِ ٱلْأَعْمَى: the eye of a blind person
key_terms.لِسَانِ ٱلْأَخْرَسِ: the tongue of a mute person

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due for the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, or the private part of a young boy in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states specific legal rulings concerning diyah for injuries to certain organs and bodily capacities. It assigns one-third of the full diyah for the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, and the private part and testicles of a free eunuch, while assigning the full diyah for the private part of a young boy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5281 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub from Buraid Al-Ijli from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"For the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, and the private parts and testicles of a free eunuch, one-third of the full blood money (diyya) is due.
However, for the private part of a young boy, the full blood money is due."
